note: THE RIGHTS COLUMN. Ruling 74, F5 Part 3, built in F6 on 2026-09-06. Ruling 74 lets an in-copyright source be cited and quoted under four conditions declared in the record, and the third is that the rights position is stated verbatim -- and where a source states no terms, that the record says THAT, in those words. Nothing could read the column: `citation_original` is free prose, ingest.verify does not open it, and F6_START's debt list records the consequence -- 'the corpus sits in at least four rights states and the position is recoverable only by reading 40 records by hand.'
why_this_file_is_not_inside_the_records: For data/corpus_tiers.json's reason, one file over and unchanged: a `rights` key on a seed record would move that record's content_hash and therefore corpus_digest, and doing it to all 40 at once would re-hash the whole corpus to add a field that describes the SOURCE rather than the text. The sidecar lives in data/ where no corpus walk reaches it -- iter_seed_records refuses any .json under the corpus directory that is not at region/record.json depth.
why_it_is_not_DERIVED_from_citation_orig: Because it cannot be, and the attempt is FINDING 69's defect with a regular expression in front of it. citation_original is prose written by a curator; a matcher over it would find the word `open` in a sentence about REACHABILITY -- which is exactly the two-facts-one-word failure FINDING 69 records, four times, in this repository's own hunt documents. A rights position is READ BY A PERSON, off the object, and this file records who read it and when. What the instrument checks is the SHAPE and the COVERAGE, never the content.

vocabulary.open_licence_stated: A named open licence, stated on the object read and quoted verbatim below.
vocabulary.permission_stated_no_licence: The source states, in its own words, what may be done with its content, and names NO LICENCE. ADDED IN F6 BY A CASE rather than declared in advance: Riksantikvarieambetet's Runor says the database's information may be reused with attribution and names no licence anywhere. `open_licence_stated` would have been a lie, `states_no_terms` the opposite lie, and `unread` would have thrown away a reading that was made. FINDING 69 separated REACHABLE from LICENSED; this separates LICENSED UNDER A NAMED LICENCE from PERMITTED IN PROSE. The permission is quoted verbatim like any other stated position.
vocabulary.public_domain: Out of copyright by age, or carrying a public-domain mark, stated on the object read.
vocabulary.all_rights_reserved: A reserved-rights statement. Ruling 74's four conditions apply in full or the source is not taken.
vocabulary.states_no_terms: The object was reached and states no terms of any kind. Ruling 74: the record says THAT, in those words. NOT the same as `unread` -- this is a reading whose answer was nothing, and that is the answer.
vocabulary.two_positions_stated: The source states MORE THAN ONE rights position and they do not agree. parsigdatabase.com is the first: an attribution-only permission and an all-rights-reserved notice, five lines apart in the same footer. The record quotes both, verbatim, in the order they appear, and adjudicates neither.
vocabulary.unread: NOBODY HAS READ THIS SOURCE'S RIGHTS POSITION SINCE FINDING 69. Not a state of the source: a state of this project's knowledge of it. FINDING 69, F5 Part 3: 'Every other licence claim in this repository is now suspect until re-read.' This is that sentence made countable.

why_unread_is_the_default_and_not_a_gues: Thirty-eight of forty records enter this file as `unread`, and the temptation to fill them from the prose already in citation_original is the whole reason the file exists. FINDING 69 was produced by two licence claims that were WRONG in opposite directions in a single session -- one recorded reachability as a licence, one verified a licence against the wrong object. A column populated from those same sentences would inherit both errors and print them as a table. An unread cell is a debt with a name; a guessed cell is a finding waiting.

That is half of FINDING 69: a licence verified against the wrong object. The issue date 2021-04-26 that F5_CANDIDATES.md carries was on neither page and is not asserted anywhere.

arabia-06-syllaeus.note: The other half of FINDING 69, from the opposite direction. F5_CANDIDATES.md recorded this source as 'the one verified open'. It is REACHABLE -- a deposit in the Hungarian Academy of Sciences' repository at real.mtak.hu, free to read under a repository policy -- and it is under NO Creative Commons licence at all. stated_verbatim: The use of the data of this site with mentioning the source is unrestricted.
persia-06-shahrestaniha.note: Both sentences sit in the footer of every page of the site, five lines apart, and they do not agree. The Persian interface prints the first as استفاده از داده‌های این سایت با ذکر منبع بلامانع است. NEITHER IS ADJUDICATED. The record quotes both, in the order they appear, and credits the source by name -- which is the one thing the first sentence actually asks for. The EDITED TEXT behind the transcription is Jamasp-Asana 1897-1913 and is public domain, cited section by section on the page, so the source-text side of the record does not rest on either sentence.

scandinavia-06-tjurko-bracteate.stated_verbatim: Information om databasen får gärna återanvändas på webbsidor, men vi är tacksamma om källan alltid anges med en hänvisning till Samnordisk runtextdatabas och en länk till objektets stabila URI på kulturarvsdata.se, alltså t.ex.: ”Runinskrift N 2 i Samnordisk runtextdatabas 2020, Institutionen för nordiska språk, Uppsala universitet. http://kulturarvsdata.se/uu/srdb/9dc30dec-30c2-4d6d-9851-6ebdabc490ba ”.
scandinavia-06-tjurko-bracteate.note: Riksantikvarieambetet's own citation guidance for the runtext database, published 2021-02-10, updated 2023-06-15. It permits reuse and asks for attribution plus a link to the stable kulturarvsdata.se URI. IT NAMES NO LICENCE ANYWHERE REACHED. This is the cell that made the seventh position necessary -- see the vocabulary. The attribution asked for is given in the record's citation and translation_source, in the shape the source asks for it.

scandinavia-07-rycksta-grikkium.stated_verbatim: Information om databasen får gärna återanvändas på webbsidor, men vi är tacksamma om källan alltid anges med en hänvisning till Samnordisk runtextdatabas och en länk till objektets stabila URI på kulturarvsdata.se, alltså t.ex.: ”Runinskrift N 2 i Samnordisk runtextdatabas 2020, Institutionen för nordiska språk, Uppsala universitet. http://kulturarvsdata.se/uu/srdb/9dc30dec-30c2-4d6d-9851-6ebdabc490ba ”.
scandinavia-07-rycksta-grikkium.note: The same Riksantikvarieambetet citation guidance as scandinavia-06-tjurko-bracteate, read off the same page on the same day. TWO RECORDS UNDER ONE READING, and that is stated rather than left to look like two independent verifications: one person read one page once, and both cells rest on it.

africa-06-ezana-rie189.stated_verbatim: ©2013 George Hatke. Distributed under the terms of the Creative Commons Attribution Non-Commercial License.
africa-06-ezana-rie189.note: The front matter of the open-access edition in the NYU Library's Ancient World Digital Library, in partnership with ISAW. A NAMED LICENCE WITH NO VERSION NUMBER: the page says "the Creative Commons Attribution Non-Commercial License" and prints no 2.0/3.0/4.0 and no link to a deed, and this cell records the string as printed rather than supplying one. The non-commercial condition is met by the use and the attribution condition by the record's citation and translation_source. FIRST open_licence_stated cell in this corpus whose licence imposes a condition on the USE rather than only on the citation.

arabia-07-cih541.stated_verbatim: The above license applies to the data in this record, but not to any images displayed. The images are the property of third parties and are either used with permission or reproduced from publications (see the credits below each image).
arabia-07-cih541.note: The licence mark printed on the epigraph record itself is CC BY 4.0, with the quoted sentence beside it carving images out of it. READ TWICE BY TWO DIFFERENT AGENTS: a person read this record's licence in F5 Part 3's browser pass 3 on 2026-09-05 and recorded it in F5_PART3_BROWSER_PASSES.md, and this session read it again on the page on 2026-09-06 before writing the cell. That is why read_by is curator_and_model and not model. A VERSIONED LICENCE, unlike africa-06-ezana-rie189's, which names the licence and prints no version -- the column records what each source printed.

eastasia-08-songshi-fulin.stated_verbatim: Unless otherwise indicated the specific electronic form of the document is copyright. Permission is granted for electronic copying, distribution in print form for educational purposes and personal use. If you do reduplicate the document, indicate the source. No permission is granted for commercial use of the Sourcebook.
eastasia-08-songshi-fulin.note: THIS CELL IS FOR THE TRANSLATION AND NOT FOR THE SOURCE TEXT, and the record uses two sources. The English is the Internet East Asian History Sourcebook's electronic form of Hirth 1885 as modified by Jerome S. Arkenberg: reuse permitted in prose for educational and personal use, attribution asked for, commercial use refused, AND NO LICENCE NAMED ANYWHERE REACHED -- which is the seventh position exactly. The Chinese is Kanripo's, recorded by eastasia-05-liangshu-qin-lun as CC BY-SA 4.0; that reading was INHERITED and not re-read this session, which is why this cell does not claim it. A record whose two halves have two rights positions is a case this column cannot yet express, and it is named here rather than resolved by picking the more flattering one.

africa-07-cosmas-sasu.stated_verbatim: This text was transcribed by Roger Pearse, 2003.  All material on this page is in the public domain - copy freely.
africa-07-cosmas-sasu.note: THE FIRST public_domain CELL IN THIS CORPUS. Six of the seven positions had been exercised and this one had not. It is not open_licence_stated because no licence is named -- a public-domain dedication is not a licence and CC0 is not mentioned anywhere reached -- and it is not states_no_terms because the source DOES state terms: it states that the material is public domain and invites copying. The underlying translation, McCrindle 1897, is out of copyright on its own, so ruling 74 is not invoked at all; this is the case ruling 74 needs to be able to tell itself apart from.

persia-07-met-ewer-anahita.stated_verbatim: In February 2017, The Met introduced its Open Access Initiative, which makes images of public-domain artworks and basic data on all accessioned works in its collection available for unrestricted use under Creative Commons Zero (CC0).
persia-07-met-ewer-anahita.note:
THE GRANT IS CONDITIONAL AND THE CONDITION WAS CHECKED FOR THIS OBJECT. data/met-licence-declaration.txt, written for Block B4's distractor fetch on 2026-08-14, states it: the CC0 designation applies to public-domain artworks only and is a property of the individual object record, not of the collection or the API. The Met's own object-level flag was read for 67.10a, b on 2026-09-06 -- collectionapi.metmuseum.org/public/collection/v1/objects/325865 returns "isPublicDomain": true -- and the object page prints the line `Public Domain` directly beneath the description. Both are the STATUS the CC0 grant rests on, not a second position.

THE EXISTING DECLARATION WAS NOT INHERITED, BECAUSE ITS OWN SCOPE EXCLUDES THIS USE. It says Met object descriptions in this project "are used as DISTRACTORS ... never cited, never translated, never placed on the map, and never presented as evidence." This is the first Met object in the SEED corpus and it is cited, placed and presented as evidence, so the page was re-read for this scope. FINDING 69 is what an inherited licence reading costs.

NOT public_domain: a licence is named, and africa-07-cosmas-sasu is that position precisely because none is.

arabia-08-walters-marib-pediment.licence: GNU Free Documentation License (no version named on the page)
arabia-08-walters-marib-pediment.stated_verbatim: Because the Walters owns or has jurisdiction over the objects in its collection and owns or customarily obtains the rights to any imaging of its collection objects, it has adopted the Creative Commons Zero: No Rights Reserved or CC0 license to waive copyright and allow for unrestricted use of digital images and metadata by any person, for any purpose. The longer text descriptions about the artworks on this website are released under the GNU Free Documentation License.
arabia-08-walters-marib-pediment.note:
THE LICENCE THE OBJECT PAGE ADVERTISES IS NOT THE LICENCE THAT COVERS THIS RECORD'S TEXT -- FINDING 87. art.thewalters.org/object/21.74/ carries eleven `Creative Commons License` badges, every one beside a `Download Image` control and every one linking to creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/. A reader of the object page alone would record this cell as CC0. The policy page's second sentence assigns the LONGER TEXT DESCRIPTIONS -- which is exactly the 700 characters this record quotes -- to the GNU Free Documentation License instead. The CC0 grant covers images and metadata.

NO VERSION IS NAMED and the cell records what is printed rather than levelling it, as F6 did for an open_licence_stated licence that named no version either.

NOT two_positions_stated: the page states two licences over two different bodies of material and says which is which, so it is one position per thing and the record knows which thing it took. two_positions_stated is for material with two positions asserted over IT, which eastasia-08-songshi-fulin has and this does not.

southasia-07-bm-claudius-aureus.stated_verbatim: © 2026 The Trustees of the British Museum
southasia-07-bm-claudius-aureus.note:
THE FLATTERING READING WAS AVAILABLE AND IS REFUSED. britishmuseum.org/terms-use/copyright-and-permissions says the Museum "increasingly intend[s] to release content on our website under a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0) licence" and, immediately after, that "The Creative Commons licence does not apply to everything on our website. Content that is published under the Creative Commons licence will be marked with the following logo". THE MARKING WAS LOOKED FOR ON THIS PAGE AND IS NOT THERE: the rendered document was searched on 2026-09-06 for `Creative Commons`, for `CC BY`, and for any anchor href containing `creativecommons` -- zero of each, in the full HTML and not only the visible text. One copyright line and no badge, so the site-level intent is not asserted over this record.

SECOND CELL IN THIS TRANCHE WHERE THE ADVERTISED READING WAS WRONG, AND IN THE OPPOSITE DIRECTION TO THE FIRST. arabia-08-walters-marib-pediment's object page advertises CC0 over material that is not the text this corpus takes (FINDING 87); this page advertises nothing and a site-level licence exists that does not reach it. FINDING 69 came from two licence claims wrong in opposite directions in one session, which is why the column records the direction of each rather than an average.

COUNTED, NOT GATED. all_rights_reserved is a statement about what the source said and not a verdict on whether 183 characters of catalogue description may be quoted in a research corpus.

seasia-08-pong-tuk-lamp.note:
THE FIRST states_no_terms CELL IN THIS CORPUS, and F7_START.md said all seven positions had been exercised -- FINDING 88. Six had; this is the seventh.

No stated_verbatim, because the position may not carry a quotation and there is nothing to quote. WHAT WAS LOOKED AT on 2026-09-06: the object page, the site's About us page, and the footer of both. The only copyright line anywhere is `© 2009-2014 by GPIUTMD`, which sits beneath a Joomla login block and names a TEMPLATE VENDOR -- a credit for the site's design, not the Fine Arts Department saying anything about reuse of its catalogue text. No terms page, no permissions page, no licence, no reuse statement; the navigation offers About us, Service, Organization and Contact us and nothing else.

WHY NOT all_rights_reserved: that position asserts what a source SAID and must quote it verbatim, and the only quotable line is a third party's. Recording GPIUTMD's credit as the Bangkok National Museum's rights position would attribute a claim to a source that does not make it -- FINDING 69's error in the direction where a curator invents a restriction rather than a permission.

SEARCH BOUNDARY: only the English-language side of the site was read. The Thai pages were not opened and no negative is recorded against them.

seasia-09-oc-eo-unesco.licence: Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 3.0 IGO -- stated for `© UNESCO` content, and whether it reaches this text is the unsettled question
stated_verbatim: All photographs and other elements of the UNESCO World Heritage Centre website are protected by international treaties on intellectual property and other applicable laws. The elements it displays may not be copied or retransmitted by any means without explicit authorisation from the World Heritage Centre or the copyright holders.
The sole responsibility for the content of each Tentative List lies with the State Party concerned.
seasia-09-oc-eo-unesco.note:
SECOND two_positions_stated CELL IN THE CORPUS AND THE FIRST WHERE ONE PUBLISHER ASSERTS BOTH OVER ONE TEXT. persia-06-shahrestaniha's two sentences sit five lines apart in one footer; eastasia-08-songshi-fulin's came from two different sites covering two halves of one record. Here whc.unesco.org states a blanket restriction over everything it displays AND a CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO licence over `© UNESCO` content, and everything turns on which of those a State Party's tentative-list submission is.

THE THREE QUOTATIONS, IN THE ORDER THEY APPEAR. The first two are on https://whc.unesco.org/en/disclaimer/ -- the blanket restriction under `Images Policy`, then the licence, which is the `License / Read Usage Terms` cell of the row headed `© UNESCO` in a table whose other row is headed `non © UNESCO`. THE THIRD IS ON THE RECORD PAGE ITSELF and is what makes the first two ambiguous rather than complementary: it names somebody other than UNESCO as solely responsible for this text.

WHAT PULLS EACH WAY. The record page's footer asserts `© UNESCO World Heritage Centre 1992-2026`. The disclaimer assigns sole responsibility for the content to the State Party. The terms table's `non © UNESCO` row lists nomination files and does not name tentative lists. Responsibility is not ownership, and the page nowhere says which side of its own table this text falls on. NEITHER IS ADJUDICATED, which is what this position is for.

WHAT THIS RECORD DOES: takes the safer reading, treats the excerpt as covered by the blanket restriction rather than by the licence, and does not assert that CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO reaches it. COUNTED, NOT GATED.

stated_verbatim: Unless otherwise indicated the specific electronic form of the document is copyright. Permission is granted for electronic copying, distribution in print form for educational purposes and personal use. If you do reduplicate the document, indicate the source. No permission is granted for commercial use of the Sourcebook.
eastasia-09-jiutangshu-fulin.note:
THIRD two_positions_stated CELL IN THE CORPUS, and the two statements are about the same text rather than about two halves of a record. The first grants electronic copying and print distribution for educational and personal use, asks for the source to be indicated, and refuses commercial use. The second asserts copyright over `any modernization` with no grant attached -- and on THIS record the modernization IS the text.

WHY THIS DIFFERS FROM eastasia-08-songshi-fulin's CELL ON THE SAME URL. That cell quotes the first statement and not the second, and was right to: the Sourcebook supplied one half of a bilingual record whose Chinese came from Kanripo. Here the record is nothing but the modernized English, so the second statement lands on it directly. NOBODY RE-CURATES A RECORD; eastasia-08's cell stands. This is a different question asked of the same page, not a correction of it.

NEITHER IS ADJUDICATED. The source is credited by name, which is the one thing the first statement asks for.

THE UNDERLYING TRANSLATION IS PUBLIC DOMAIN ON ITS OWN -- Hirth 1885, archive.org `chinaandromanor00hirtgoog`, `possible-copyright-status: NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT` -- and that does not resolve the cell, because what this record holds is not Hirth 1885 as printed. See the record's translation_source for what the comparison found.

southasia-06-cosmas-taprobane.stated_verbatim: This text was transcribed by Roger Pearse, 2003.  All material on this page is in the public domain - copy freely.
southasia-06-cosmas-taprobane.note:
SECOND public_domain CELL IN THE CORPUS, after africa-07-cosmas-sasu, and it is the same sentence on a DIFFERENT PAGE of the same site -- F6 read it off cosmas_02_book2.htm and this was read off cosmas_11_book11.htm on 2026-09-06. READ AGAIN RATHER THAN INHERITED: the two pages could have differed and did not.

Not open_licence_stated because no licence is named and a public-domain dedication is not a licence. Not states_no_terms because the source DOES state terms -- that the material is public domain and may be copied freely -- which is a position and not a silence; seasia-08-pong-tuk-lamp, curated in this same tranche, is what a real silence looks like.

The underlying translation, McCrindle 1897, is out of copyright on its own (published 1897, translator died 1913), so ruling 74's conditions are not invoked.
